New York Schools and County Socioeconomic Conditions

Yifei Bu

Introduction

This analysis explores how socioeconomic conditions are related to academic performance in New York State schools. I focus on county poverty, student participation in free or reduced-price lunch programs, and standardized Math and ELA performance. # Data and Cleaning

The analysis uses school-level data from the New York State Department of Education and county-level data from the American Community Survey.

Missing values originally coded as -99 were converted to NA. Invalid percentage values were also treated as missing. Because New York State test scales changed over time, Math and ELA scores were standardized within each year using z-scores.

Poverty Groups

Counties were divided into three approximately equal-sized groups within each year based on their poverty rate. Counties in the lowest third were classified as low poverty, those in the middle third as medium poverty, and those in the highest third as high poverty.

Lunch Assistance and Academic Performance

Key Findings

The analysis shows clear socioeconomic differences in school outcomes. Schools serving larger shares of students receiving free or reduced-price lunch tend to have lower standardized test performance. Academic performance also differs across county poverty groups.

These results describe associations in the data and should not be interpreted as evidence that poverty or lunch-program participation directly causes differences in test scores.
